Player forecasts are well calibrated. On the holdout, predicted buckets landed within about 3 points of actual hit rates. The test used who actually played, so live forecasts will be slightly worse because inactives are unknown in advance.

Game lines show no edge. Closing spread MAE was 9.70 points vs 10.11 for our line, and the fitted weight on our line was about zero. Closing totals: 10.18 vs 10.61. So game sides default to pass.

Prop edges are unproven. Calibration shows the probabilities are honest. It does not show they beat DraftKings, because no historical prop lines were available to test against. The edges here are leads to price-check.

2026 holdout, all markets. Dots near the dashed line mean a forecast of X% hit about X% of the time. Bigger dots hold more forecasts.

Data gaps

  • Prop prices: ESPN's DraftKings feed gives lines and milestone levels but no prices. Moneyline, spread and total prices are real. Prop edges assume -110, and each pick shows a minimum acceptable price.
  • 2026 coverage: man/zone and coverage shells have no free 2026 feed. 2025 charting stands in, labeled every time, and flagged when a head coach changed. Coordinator changes are not tracked.
  • Alignment and routes: 2026 slot/wide alignment and routes run are paid data. Target side, depth and 2025 route targets stand in. Press rate, shadow rate, tackle-vs-edge win rate, and run-scheme splits are left out.
  • Under-pressure splits: team pressure rates are 2026 (PFR). Individual QB pressure splits are 2025. Blitz splits are 2026 (FTN).
  • Injury odds: P(plays) values are assumptions from status and practice, not fitted estimates.

nflverse supplied play-by-play, FTN charting, PFR advanced stats, NGS, snap counts, depth charts and rosters. ESPN supplied the schedule, injuries and DraftKings lines. NWS supplied forecasts.

These are estimates, and no selection is guaranteed. After the games, run review.py to score every forecast (Phase 15).

DraftKings via ESPN, pulled Friday, Nov 13 at 11:48 AM. Sun Nov 15, 9:30 AM ET · FC Bayern Munich Stadium.

TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is ruled out. Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is officially questionable after limited practices (Patriots.com injury report, Nov 13), but Ian Rapoport reported Nov 9 that he was expected to miss the next few weeks, and ESPN says he was not in uniform Friday. Corey Kiner is next up. New England rushing lines are held out until inactives. A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is questionable after three limited practices; Hunter Henry (foot) was limited; Drake Maye (right shoulder) practiced in full (Patriots.com).

Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited all week and has no posted game status yet; Jared Goff (chest) practiced in full; Sione Vaki (ankle) did not practice (Patriots.com injury report, Nov 13).

Defensive scheme

DET defense vs NE offense: what to attack

  • DET is soft on Inter 10-19 throws to the middle (+1.83 EPA/att vs league +0.61, 17 attempts).
  • DET is soft on Deep 20+ throws to the right (+1.01 EPA/att vs league +0.39, 18 attempts).
  • Avoid Inter 10-19 throws to the left: DET allows -0.52 EPA/att vs league +0.31 (17 attempts).
  • DET gives up 94 yds/game to WR1 (most targets) (league 72).
  • DET gives up 88 yds/game to All TE (league 55).
  • Run stuffed: Outside (tackle / end) gains only 3.5 YPC on DET (league 4.5).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Rhamondre Stevenson (RB, Questionable), A.J. Brown (WR, Questionable), Hunter Henry (TE, Questionable), Charles Woods (CB, Questionable), DJ Wonnum (LB, Questionable), Sione Vaki (RB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Drake Maye and Jared Goff. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Drake Maye 170+ passing yds (91%) + Jameson Williams 10+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 83.1%, fair -491. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.7% vs 75.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Sam LaPorta 20+ receiving yds (79%) + Jared Goff 210+ passing yds (78%) + Drake Maye 210+ passing yds (77%). Joint estimate 53.9%, fair -117. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.5% vs 37.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jameson Williams 40+ receiving yds (62%) + Jared Goff 250+ passing yds (60%) + Amon-Ra St. Brown 70+ receiving yds (59%). Joint estimate 35.0%, fair +185. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.6% vs 13.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Player main lines
Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Drake Maye 170+ passing yds (91%) + Jameson Williams 10+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 83.1%, fair -491. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.7% vs 75.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Sam LaPorta 20+ receiving yds (79%) + Jared Goff 210+ passing yds (78%) + Drake Maye 210+ passing yds (77%). Joint estimate 53.9%, fair -117. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.5% vs 37.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jameson Williams 40+ receiving yds (62%) + Jared Goff 250+ passing yds (60%) + Amon-Ra St. Brown 70+ receiving yds (59%). Joint estimate 35.0%, fair +185. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.6% vs 13.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Jaydn Ott (RB, Questionable), Peter Woods (DT, Questionable), Jaylon Moore (OT, Questionable), Kendal Daniels (LB, Questionable), Cameron Thomas (DE, Questionable), Zachariah Branch (WR, Doubtful), Josh Woods (LB, Questionable), James Pearce Jr. (LB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Patrick Mahomes and Michael Penix Jr.. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Travis Kelce 10+ receiving yds (92%) + Kenneth Walker III 40+ rushing yds (90%). Joint estimate 82.1%, fair -459. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.8% vs 75.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Xavier Worthy 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Bijan Robinson 50+ rushing yds (78%) + Rashee Rice 25+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 48.6%, fair +106. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 36.4% vs 36.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jahan Dotson 15+ receiving yds (62%) + Kenneth Walker III 10+ receiving yds (61%) + Travis Kelce 40+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 22.6%, fair +342. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 16.1% vs 15.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Travis Kelce 10+ receiving yds (92%) + Kenneth Walker III 40+ rushing yds (90%). Joint estimate 82.1%, fair -459. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.8% vs 75.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Xavier Worthy 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Bijan Robinson 50+ rushing yds (78%) + Rashee Rice 25+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 48.6%, fair +106. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 36.4% vs 36.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jahan Dotson 15+ receiving yds (62%) + Kenneth Walker III 10+ receiving yds (61%) + Travis Kelce 40+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 22.6%, fair +342. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 16.1% vs 15.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Reed Blankenship (S, Questionable), Danielle Hunter (DE, Questionable), Will Anderson Jr. (DE, Questionable), Marvin Harrison Jr. (WR, Questionable), Woody Marks (RB, Questionable), Harold Fannin Jr. (TE, Questionable), Denzel Boston (WR, Questionable), Carson Schwesinger (LB, Questionable), Denzel Ward (CB, Questionable), Quincy Williams (LB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: C.J. Stroud and Deshaun Watson. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: C.J. Stroud 160+ passing yds (88%) + Deshaun Watson 150+ passing yds (86%). Joint estimate 76.0%, fair -317. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 68.0% vs 67.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: C.J. Stroud 180+ passing yds (80%) + Deshaun Watson 170+ passing yds (76%) + Nico Collins 20+ receiving yds (75%). Joint estimate 51.6%, fair -106. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 39.0% vs 34.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Nico Collins 30+ receiving yds (62%) + C.J. Stroud 220+ passing yds (58%) + Deshaun Watson 200+ passing yds (58%). Joint estimate 28.8%, fair +247. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 19.5% vs 14.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative: C.J. Stroud 160+ passing yds (88%) + Deshaun Watson 150+ passing yds (86%). Joint estimate 76.0%, fair -317. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 68.0% vs 67.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: C.J. Stroud 180+ passing yds (80%) + Deshaun Watson 170+ passing yds (76%) + Nico Collins 20+ receiving yds (75%). Joint estimate 51.6%, fair -106. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 39.0% vs 34.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Nico Collins 30+ receiving yds (62%) + C.J. Stroud 220+ passing yds (58%) + Deshaun Watson 200+ passing yds (58%). Joint estimate 28.8%, fair +247. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 19.5% vs 14.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Kirk Cousins, acquired from the Raiders on Nov 10, is expected to start at Green Bay (ESPN injury page, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13); the team has not been quoted naming him, but the depth chart lists him first. Kyler Murray (hamstring) is doubtful and week-to-week, and Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited Thursday. T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) and Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Thursday (ESPN, Nov 12-13). Cousins's 2026 history is with Las Vegas and he has had one week in this offense, so Minnesota passing and receiving lines are low confidence.

Josh Jacobs (broken finger) is out; he has surgery Friday and is expected to miss multiple weeks (Packers.com, Nov 9; ESPN, citing Matt Schneidman, Nov 12). Kaleb Johnson led the backfield with 14 carries in Week 9, and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is off the injury report (ESPN, Nov 10-11). Roles are changing, so Green Bay rushing lines are held out.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Blake Cashman (LB, Questionable), Jauan Jennings (WR, Questionable), Carson Wentz (QB, Questionable), T.J. Hockenson (TE, Questionable), Jay Ward (S, Questionable), Kevin Zeitler (G, Questionable), Travis Glover (OT, Questionable), Aaron Banks (G, Questionable), Sean Rhyan (G, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Carson Wentz and Jordan Love. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Matthew Golden 20+ receiving yds (90%) + Christian Watson 20+ receiving yds (89%). Joint estimate 80.6%, fair -415. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 71.8% vs 71.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Jordan Love 180+ passing yds (78%) + Tucker Kraft 15+ receiving yds (75%) + Christian Watson 40+ receiving yds (73%). Joint estimate 52.9%, fair -112. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 37.6% vs 30.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jordan Love 220+ passing yds (57%) + Tucker Kraft 25+ receiving yds (57%) + Savion Williams 10+ receiving yds (57%). Joint estimate 24.3%, fair +311. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 16.5% vs 12.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Matthew Golden 20+ receiving yds (90%) + Christian Watson 20+ receiving yds (89%). Joint estimate 80.6%, fair -415. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 71.8% vs 71.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Jordan Love 180+ passing yds (78%) + Tucker Kraft 15+ receiving yds (75%) + Christian Watson 40+ receiving yds (73%). Joint estimate 52.9%, fair -112. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 37.6% vs 30.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jordan Love 220+ passing yds (57%) + Tucker Kraft 25+ receiving yds (57%) + Savion Williams 10+ receiving yds (57%). Joint estimate 24.3%, fair +311. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 16.5% vs 12.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Kirk Cousins, acquired from the Raiders on Nov 10, is expected to start at Green Bay (ESPN injury page, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13); the team has not been quoted naming him, but the depth chart lists him first. Kyler Murray (hamstring) is doubtful and week-to-week, and Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited Thursday. T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) and Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Thursday (ESPN, Nov 12-13). Cousins's 2026 history is with Las Vegas and he has had one week in this offense, so Minnesota passing and receiving lines are low confidence.

Josh Jacobs (broken finger) is out; he has surgery Friday and is expected to miss multiple weeks (Packers.com, Nov 9; ESPN, citing Matt Schneidman, Nov 12). Kaleb Johnson led the backfield with 14 carries in Week 9, and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is off the injury report (ESPN, Nov 10-11). Roles are changing, so Green Bay rushing lines are held out.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Blake Cashman (LB, Questionable); Jauan Jennings (WR, Questionable); Carson Wentz (QB, Questionable); T.J. Hockenson (TE, Questionable); Jay Ward (S, Questionable); Kevin Zeitler (G, Questionable); Travis Glover (OT, Questionable); Aaron Banks (G, Questionable); Sean Rhyan (G, Questionable).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Bhayshul Tuten (RB, Questionable), Travon Walker (DE, Questionable), Jakobi Meyers (WR, Questionable), Chris Rodriguez Jr. (RB, Questionable), Tyjae Spears (RB, Questionable), Tony Pollard (RB, Questionable), Kevin Winston Jr. (S, Questionable), Cody Barton (LB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Trevor Lawrence and Cam Ward. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Trevor Lawrence 160+ passing yds (92%) + Parker Washington 15+ receiving yds (90%). Joint estimate 85.6%, fair -594. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 77.8% vs 75.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Cam Ward 150+ passing yds (79%) + Parker Washington 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Brenton Strange 20+ receiving yds (77%). Joint estimate 49.6%, fair +102. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 36.5% vs 35.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Parker Washington 50+ receiving yds (61%) + Cam Ward 180+ passing yds (60%) + Trevor Lawrence 250+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 31.2%, fair +221. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.1% vs 14.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Trevor Lawrence 160+ passing yds (92%) + Parker Washington 15+ receiving yds (90%). Joint estimate 85.6%, fair -594. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 77.8% vs 75.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Cam Ward 150+ passing yds (79%) + Parker Washington 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Brenton Strange 20+ receiving yds (77%). Joint estimate 49.6%, fair +102. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 36.5% vs 35.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Parker Washington 50+ receiving yds (61%) + Cam Ward 180+ passing yds (60%) + Trevor Lawrence 250+ passing yds (60%). Joint estimate 31.2%, fair +221. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.1% vs 14.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Chris Bell (WR, Doubtful), Jared Wayne (WR, Questionable), Will Kacmarek (TE, Questionable), Jerry Tillery (DT, Questionable), Akeem Davis-Gaither (LB, Questionable), Mo Alie-Cox (TE, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: None and Daniel Jones. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Balanced: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Player main lines
Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

MIA strengths: explosive runs on defense (#7). Weaknesses: overall EPA on defense (#32); passing EPA on defense (#32); success rate on defense (#32); 3rd downs on defense (#30); red-zone TDs on offense (#28).

IND strengths: 3rd downs on defense (#5). Weaknesses: explosive passing on defense (#32); rushing EPA on defense (#32); explosive passing on offense (#30); passing EPA on offense (#30); overall EPA on offense (#29).

Kyle McCord makes his first NFL start; Malik Willis (core muscle) went on IR Nov 10 and misses at least four games (ESPN, citing Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network, Nov 10). Miami passing history under Willis is stale, so its passing and receiving lines are low confidence. WR Chris Bell (knee) did not practice Thursday (ESPN, Nov 12).

The Colts traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Nov 10 and Alec Pierce (heel) is on IR. Coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Gould takes the slot and Deion Burks and Ashton Dulin step into larger roles (ESPN, Stephen Holder, Nov 11). Indianapolis receiving lines carry role uncertainty.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Chris Bell (WR, Doubtful); Aaron Brewer (C, Out); Jared Wayne (WR, Questionable); Darrell Baker Jr. (CB, Out); Will Kacmarek (TE, Questionable); Jerry Tillery (DT, Questionable); Akeem Davis-Gaither (LB, Questionable); Mo Alie-Cox (TE, Questionable).

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

3 · Traps

Lines that look good on a streak, a soft matchup or old QB history, where the model says otherwise.

No line here pairs a popular read with a model that disagrees.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Bobby Okereke (LB, Questionable), Taliese Fuaga (OT, Questionable), David Edwards (G, Questionable), Kelvin Banks Jr. (OT, Questionable), Quincy Riley (CB, Questionable), CJ Donaldson (RB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Bryce Young and Tyler Shough. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Tetairoa McMillan 20+ receiving yds (93%) + Jalen Coker 10+ receiving yds (92%). Joint estimate 85.1%, fair -572. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 77.8% vs 77.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Bryce Young 200+ passing yds (80%) + Tyler Shough 180+ passing yds (79%) + Tetairoa McMillan 40+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 56.5%, fair -130. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 43.5% vs 38.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Devaughn Vele 25+ receiving yds (61%) + Bryce Young 240+ passing yds (60%) + Chuba Hubbard 60+ rushing yds (60%). Joint estimate 23.3%, fair +328. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 15.6% vs 14.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Sam Franklin Jr. (S, Questionable), Dalton Kincaid (TE, Questionable), Dion Dawkins (OT, Questionable), Christian Benford (CB, Questionable), Spencer Brown (OT, Questionable), Garrett Wilson (WR, Questionable), Harrison Phillips (DT, Questionable), Nahshon Wright (CB, Questionable), Joseph Ossai (DE, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Josh Allen and Geno Smith. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Josh Allen 160+ passing yds (91%) + Omar Cooper Jr. 10+ receiving yds (89%). Joint estimate 81.0%, fair -427. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 73.1% vs 73.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Keon Coleman 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Omar Cooper Jr. 20+ receiving yds (78%) + Josh Allen 200+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 52.9%, fair -112. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 39.2% vs 35.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Ty Johnson 10+ receiving yds (62%) + James Cook 70+ rushing yds (61%) + Keon Coleman 30+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 22.7%, fair +340. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 15.7% vs 15.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Josh Allen 160+ passing yds (91%) + Omar Cooper Jr. 10+ receiving yds (89%). Joint estimate 81.0%, fair -427. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 73.1% vs 73.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Keon Coleman 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Omar Cooper Jr. 20+ receiving yds (78%) + Josh Allen 200+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 52.9%, fair -112. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 39.2% vs 35.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Ty Johnson 10+ receiving yds (62%) + James Cook 70+ rushing yds (61%) + Keon Coleman 30+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 22.7%, fair +340. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 15.7% vs 15.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Sam Darnold (quad) is out again and coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Drew Lock starts at Las Vegas (ESPN/ABC7 and Fox 13 Seattle, Nov 9; ESPN injury page, Nov 10). The depth-chart feed still lists Darnold. Lock (right elbow/oblique) was limited Thursday (ESPN, citing John Boyle of Seahawks.com, Nov 13), so if he can't go Jalen Milroe would make his first NFL start. Seattle passing and receiving lines rest on Lock's small 2026 sample. In the backfield, Zach Charbonnet took 16 carries and Jadarian Price 9 in Week 9 while Emanuel Wilson did not play a snap (ESPN, Nov 9-11). The carry-share history still credits Wilson, so Seattle rushing lines are held out.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Charles Cross (OT, Doubtful), Drew Lock (QB, Questionable), Derick Hall (LB, Questionable), Leonard Williams (DT, Questionable), Connor O'Toole (LB, Questionable), Trey Zuhn III (C, Questionable), Thomas Booker IV (DT, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Drew Lock and Fernando Mendoza. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Ashton Jeanty 15+ rushing yds (83%) + Mike Washington Jr. 15+ rushing yds (81%). Joint estimate 67.5%, fair -208. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 60.7% vs 60.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

LV strengths: 3rd downs on offense (#7). Weaknesses: explosive runs on offense (#32); rushing EPA on offense (#32); overall EPA on defense (#31); success rate on defense (#31); passing EPA on defense (#29).

Sam Darnold (quad) is out again and coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Drew Lock starts at Las Vegas (ESPN/ABC7 and Fox 13 Seattle, Nov 9; ESPN injury page, Nov 10). The depth-chart feed still lists Darnold. Lock (right elbow/oblique) was limited Thursday (ESPN, citing John Boyle of Seahawks.com, Nov 13), so if he can't go Jalen Milroe would make his first NFL start. Seattle passing and receiving lines rest on Lock's small 2026 sample. In the backfield, Zach Charbonnet took 16 carries and Jadarian Price 9 in Week 9 while Emanuel Wilson did not play a snap (ESPN, Nov 9-11). The carry-share history still credits Wilson, so Seattle rushing lines are held out.

Rookie Fernando Mendoza makes his first NFL start after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Nov 10 (ESPN, Adam Schefter, Nov 10); Aidan O'Connell is the backup (ESPN, citing The Athletic, Nov 11). Mendoza has no NFL passing sample, so Las Vegas passing and receiving lines are low confidence.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Charles Cross (OT, Doubtful); Drew Lock (QB, Questionable); Derick Hall (LB, Questionable); Leonard Williams (DT, Questionable); Connor O'Toole (LB, Questionable); Trey Zuhn III (C, Questionable); Thomas Booker IV (DT, Questionable).

DraftKings via ESPN, pulled Friday, Nov 13 at 11:48 AM. Sun Nov 15, 4:05 PM ET · State Farm Stadium.

Puka Nacua (MCL/PCL sprain, turf toe) went on IR Thursday and misses at least four games (ESPN injury page, Nov 13; TheRams.com). Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) are also on IR. Tight ends Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice and Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited (ESPN, citing Adam Caplan, Nov 13). Nacua's targets have to be redistributed, so Rams passing and receiving lines carry role uncertainty.

Rookie Carson Beck makes his first NFL start; coach Mike LaFleur confirmed it Wednesday (ESPN, citing Darren Urban of the Cardinals' site, Nov 11). Gardner Minshew (elbow, IR) is out for the season, and WRs Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are on IR (ESPN). Arizona passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Backfield: Jeremiyah Love and James Conner remain on IR, and Conner won't return this week (ESPN). Bam Knight (concussion) missed Week 9, when Tyler Allgeier took 17 carries; Knight practiced in full Thursday and is listed questionable (ESPN, citing the Cardinals' site, Nov 13). Arizona rushing lines are held out.

LA QB vs ARI rush

Puka Nacua (MCL/PCL sprain, turf toe) went on IR Thursday and misses at least four games (ESPN injury page, Nov 13; TheRams.com). Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) are also on IR. Tight ends Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice and Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited (ESPN, citing Adam Caplan, Nov 13). Nacua's targets have to be redistributed, so Rams passing and receiving lines carry role uncertainty.

Matthew Stafford: 357 dropbacks in 2026, +0.05 EPA/db, CPOE 0.0, time to throw 2.69s, intended air yards 7.6, sack rate 3.6%, turnover-worthy throws 4.1%. Pressure-to-sack rate in 2025: 15.4%. 2026 under-pressure splits are not free, so 2025 stands in and blitz splits come from 2026 charting.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Trent McDuffie (CB, Questionable), Davis Allen (TE, Questionable), Colby Parkinson (TE, Questionable), Tyler Higbee (TE, Questionable), Hjalte Froholdt (C, Questionable), Jayden Williams (OT, Questionable), Andrew Wingard (S, Questionable), Bam Knight (RB, Questionable), Darius Robinson (DE, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Matthew Stafford and None. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Balanced: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Executive summary Predictive

LA25.1
ARI15.8
Predicted winnerLA 78%
MarketLAR -9.5, O/U 39.5
Our independent lineLA 27.3, ARI 18.8
Most likely scriptB: LA controls (56%)

LA strengths: passing EPA on defense (#3); 3rd downs on defense (#4); overall EPA on defense (#4); rushing EPA on defense (#4); explosive runs on offense (#5). Weaknesses: explosive passing on offense (#26).

ARI strengths: none in the top 7. Weaknesses: explosive passing on offense (#31); passing EPA on defense (#31); red-zone TDs on offense (#30); overall EPA on defense (#27); red-zone TDs on defense (#27).

Puka Nacua (MCL/PCL sprain, turf toe) went on IR Thursday and misses at least four games (ESPN injury page, Nov 13; TheRams.com). Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) are also on IR. Tight ends Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice and Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited (ESPN, citing Adam Caplan, Nov 13). Nacua's targets have to be redistributed, so Rams passing and receiving lines carry role uncertainty.

Rookie Carson Beck makes his first NFL start; coach Mike LaFleur confirmed it Wednesday (ESPN, citing Darren Urban of the Cardinals' site, Nov 11). Gardner Minshew (elbow, IR) is out for the season, and WRs Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are on IR (ESPN). Arizona passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Backfield: Jeremiyah Love and James Conner remain on IR, and Conner won't return this week (ESPN). Bam Knight (concussion) missed Week 9, when Tyler Allgeier took 17 carries; Knight practiced in full Thursday and is listed questionable (ESPN, citing the Cardinals' site, Nov 13). Arizona rushing lines are held out.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Trent McDuffie (CB, Questionable); Davis Allen (TE, Questionable); Colby Parkinson (TE, Questionable); Tyler Higbee (TE, Questionable); Hjalte Froholdt (C, Questionable); Jayden Williams (OT, Questionable); Andrew Wingard (S, Questionable); Bam Knight (RB, Questionable); Darius Robinson (DE, Questionable).

  • DAL is soft on Short 0-9 throws to the middle (+0.34 EPA/att vs league +0.07, 34 attempts).
  • Avoid Deep 20+ throws to the left: DAL allows +0.01 EPA/att vs league +0.33 (17 attempts).
  • Run lane: Outside (tackle / end) gains 6.1 YPC on DAL (league 4.5).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

3 · Traps

No line here pairs a popular read with a model that disagrees.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Trent Williams (OT, Questionable), Dre Greenlaw (LB, Questionable), Mike Evans (WR, Questionable), Deebo Samuel Sr. (WR, Questionable), Jonathan Mingo (WR, Questionable), KaVontae Turpin (WR, Questionable), Juanyeh Thomas (S, Questionable), Alijah Clark (S, Questionable), George Pickens (WR, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Brock Purdy and Dak Prescott. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: CeeDee Lamb 30+ receiving yds (93%) + Javonte Williams 30+ rushing yds (93%). Joint estimate 86.4%, fair -635. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 81.1% vs 81.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Dak Prescott 200+ passing yds (80%) + Christian McCaffrey 10+ receiving yds (78%) + Brock Purdy 200+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 53.5%, fair -115. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.2% vs 37.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Javonte Williams 63+ rushing yds (61%) + Dak Prescott 240+ passing yds (60%) + Christian McCaffrey 20+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 23.7%, fair +322. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 15.9% vs 14.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: CeeDee Lamb 30+ receiving yds (93%) + Javonte Williams 30+ rushing yds (93%). Joint estimate 86.4%, fair -635. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 81.1% vs 81.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Dak Prescott 200+ passing yds (80%) + Christian McCaffrey 10+ receiving yds (78%) + Brock Purdy 200+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 53.5%, fair -115. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.2% vs 37.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Javonte Williams 63+ rushing yds (61%) + Dak Prescott 240+ passing yds (60%) + Christian McCaffrey 20+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 23.7%, fair +322. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 15.9% vs 14.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice Thursday; Kyle Shanahan called him 'real close' (ESPN, citing David Lombardi, Nov 13). Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was limited, and Brandon Aiyuk is on a roster exemption and out. Keenan Allen was acquired Nov 10 and has no role history with San Francisco (ESPN).

Tyler Goodson (ACL/MCL sprains) and Jake Ferguson (knee) are out (ESPN, citing Todd Archer and the Cowboys' site, Nov 9-10). George Pickens (hamstring) and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) were limited Thursday and Jonathan Mingo (ankle/foot) did not practice (ESPN, citing Jon Machota, Nov 12-13).

Key injuries and uncertainties: Trent Williams (OT, Questionable); Dre Greenlaw (LB, Questionable); Mike Evans (WR, Questionable); Deebo Samuel Sr. (WR, Questionable); Jonathan Mingo (WR, Questionable); KaVontae Turpin (WR, Questionable); Juanyeh Thomas (S, Questionable); Alijah Clark (S, Questionable); George Pickens (WR, Questionable).

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Kyle Dugger (S, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Aaron Rodgers and Joe Burrow. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Chase Brown 15+ rushing yds (93%) + Jaylen Warren 25+ rushing yds (89%). Joint estimate 82.5%, fair -471. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 78.0% vs 78.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Joe Burrow 220+ passing yds (80%) + Aaron Rodgers 180+ passing yds (79%) + DK Metcalf 25+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 56.0%, fair -127. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 43.1% vs 38.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Joe Burrow 260+ passing yds (62%) + Jaylen Warren 15+ receiving yds (61%) + Samaje Perine 19+ rushing yds (61%). Joint estimate 24.1%, fair +315. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 18.3% vs 17.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Chase Brown 15+ rushing yds (93%) + Jaylen Warren 25+ rushing yds (89%). Joint estimate 82.5%, fair -471. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 78.0% vs 78.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Joe Burrow 220+ passing yds (80%) + Aaron Rodgers 180+ passing yds (79%) + DK Metcalf 25+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 56.0%, fair -127. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 43.1% vs 38.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Joe Burrow 260+ passing yds (62%) + Jaylen Warren 15+ receiving yds (61%) + Samaje Perine 19+ rushing yds (61%). Joint estimate 24.1%, fair +315. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 18.3% vs 17.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.
